import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 298

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/298](https://www.erdosproblems.com/298)
- [Bl21] Bloom, T. F., On a density conjecture about unit fractions. arXiv:2112.03726 (2021).
-/

namespace Erdos298

/--
Does every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ of positive density contain some finite $S \subset A$ such that
$\sum_{n \in S} \frac{1}{n} = 1$?

The answer is yes, proved by Bloom [Bl21] (even if 'positive density' is interpreted as 'positive
upper density', which is likely what Erdős intended).

The theorem below uses the positive-upper-density interpretation; the literal natural-density
interpretation is recorded separately.

This was formalized in Lean 3 by Bloom and Mehta.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using other_system at "https://github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions/blob/master/src/final_results.lean"]
theorem erdos_298 : answer(True) ↔ (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A → 0 < A.upperDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1) := by
  sorry

/--
The literal natural-density interpretation of Erdős Problem 298 follows from [Bl21].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_298.variants.natural_density : answer(True) ↔ (∀ (A : Set ℕ), 0 ∉ A →
    A.HasPosDensity →
    ∃ (S : Finset ℕ), ↑S ⊆ A ∧ ∑ n ∈ S, (1 / n : ℚ) = 1) := by
  sorry

end Erdos298

reformulations.difference: Set.upperDensity counts A ∩ [0,N) and divides by N; Bloom's paper defines upper density using A ∩ [1,N].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under 0 ∉ A, the numerator counts differ only by whether N belongs to A. For N > 0 the quotients therefore differ by at most 1/N, which tends to zero, so their limsups coincide. The N = 0 default is irrelevant. The cited Lean 3 proof actually uses the same endpoint convention as the repository; equality with its filtered-Finset counting formula was proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: HasPosDensity requires convergence to a positive real number, whereas Bloom describes natural density through coinciding lower and upper densities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The partial-density sequence lies in [0,1]. Thus it converges to a positive number exactly when its lower and upper limits coincide and the upper limit is positive. Review298.hasPosDensity_iff_liminf_limsup proves A.HasPosDensity ↔ 0 < A.upperDensity ∧ A.lowerDensity = A.upperDensity.
